repo.description:
### Summary

The legacy `where` query parameter interpolated the comparison value into raw SQL on PostgreSQL data sources, allowing an authenticated user with read access to run arbitrary read queries against the underlying database.

### Details

When parsing a legacy filter of the form `(field,like,value)`, `CustomKnex.ts` bound the column reference as a parameter but wrapped the comparison value in a single-quoted SQL literal built by string concatenation, with no escaping. A single quote in the value closed the literal and the remainder of the value became query syntax. Only the PostgreSQL branch was affected - the operator itself came from a fixed mapping table and never from the request, and the fallback branch used for other clients already parameterised the value.

### Impact

Any authenticated user with data-read permission on a PostgreSQL-backed base, including the Viewer role, could read data well beyond their granted scope: other tables and schemas in the same database, rows excluded by view filters, and columns hidden by field visibility. The injection point is a read query and PostgreSQL's parameterised protocol rejects additional statements, so the flaw did not permit data modification.

### Credit

This issue was reported by [@tikket1](https://github.com/tikket1).
repo.summary: SQL Injection via Legacy Query Filter on PostgreSQL
